question: Does Sneak Attack work with a thrown dagger?
expected_answer: Yes. Sneak Attack requires the attack to use a finesse or a ranged weapon, and a dagger has the finesse property — which it keeps when thrown. The other Sneak Attack conditions still apply (advantage on the attack roll, or an enemy of the target within 5 feet).

question: How much damage does a Fireball do?
expected_answer: 8d6 fire damage to each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking half as much damage on a success. Cast with a slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 per slot level above 3rd.

question: What's the save DC for a Fireball cast by a 5th-level wizard with 16 Intelligence?
grounding: Spellcasting > Casting a Spell > Saving Throws
Wizard > The Wizard > Spellcasting > Spellcasting Ability
expected_answer: DC 14. The spell save DC is 8 + spellcasting ability modifier + proficiency bonus. Intelligence is the wizard's spellcasting ability, 16 Intelligence gives a +3 modifier, and a 5th-level character has a +3 proficiency bonus: 8 + 3 + 3 = 14.

question: Can I cast two levelled spells in the same turn?
grounding: Spellcasting > Casting a Spell > Casting Time > Bonus Action
expected_answer: No. If you cast a spell as a bonus action, you can't cast another spell during the same turn except a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action. Since a levelled spell cast with your action plus a levelled spell cast as a bonus action is the only way to attempt two in one turn, two levelled spells in a turn is not possible.

question: What happens to a creature that is grappled?
expected_answer: A grappled creature's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. The condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated, or if an effect removes the grappled creature from the reach of the grappler or grappling effect.

question: How far can a party travel in a day at a normal pace?
expected_answer: 24 miles per day at a normal pace, which assumes 8 hours of travel at 3 miles per hour. A fast pace covers 30 miles per day and a slow pace 18. Travelling beyond 8 hours is a forced march and risks exhaustion.

question: How does the Lucky feat work?
expected_answer: The SRD does not cover the Lucky feat; the only feat it includes is Grappler. The app should say so rather than answering. Note that the SRD does describe a halfling racial trait also called Lucky (reroll a 1 on the d20), which is a different rule — presenting it as the feat would be a wrong answer, not a refusal.

question: How do death saving throws work?
grounding: Damage and Healing > Dropping to 0 Hit Points > Death Saving Throws
expected_answer: Whenever you start your turn at 0 hit points you roll a d20 with no ability modifier. 10 or higher is a success, lower is a failure. Three successes stabilise you; three failures kill you, and they need not be consecutive. Rolling a 1 counts as two failures and rolling a 20 restores you to 1 hit point. Taking damage at 0 hit points causes a failure, or two from a critical hit. Both counts reset when you regain hit points or become stable.

question: When do I provoke an opportunity attack?
grounding: Making an Attack > Melee Attacks > Opportunity Attacks
expected_answer: You provoke when you move out of the reach of a hostile creature that can see you. That creature uses its reaction to make one melee attack, resolved right before you leave its reach. You do not provoke if you take the Disengage action, if you teleport, or if something else moves you without using your own movement, action, or reaction.

question: What do you get from a long rest?
expected_answer: A long rest is at least 8 hours of sleep or light activity. At the end of it a character regains all lost hit points and regains spent Hit Dice up to half their total number of Hit Dice, minimum one. A character cannot benefit from more than one long rest in 24 hours and must have at least 1 hit point when the rest begins. Interruption by at least an hour of strenuous activity means the rest must be started again.

question: What happens if I have both advantage and disadvantage on the same roll?
grounding: Using Ability Scores > Advantage and Disadvantage
expected_answer: They cancel out and you roll a single d20 with neither. This holds no matter how many sources are involved, so several sources of disadvantage against one source of advantage still results in a plain roll. Multiple sources on the same side never stack either: you never roll more than one extra d20.

question: What features does the Eldritch Knight martial archetype give a fighter?
expected_answer: The SRD does not cover the Eldritch Knight. The only martial archetype it includes is the Champion. The app should say the SRD does not cover it rather than describing Champion features in its place.

question: What does the spell Silvery Barbs do?
expected_answer: The SRD does not contain a spell called Silvery Barbs. The app should say so rather than inventing an effect for it.

question: What do you recover on a short rest?
expected_answer: Hit points, by spending Hit Dice. A short rest is at least 1 hour of light activity, and at the end of it you may spend one or more Hit Dice up to your maximum, which equals your level. For each die spent you roll it, add your Constitution modifier, and regain that many hit points, deciding whether to spend another after each roll. Spent Hit Dice are only regained on a long rest.

question: What does an adult red dragon's fire breath do?
grounding: Monsters (D) > Red Dragon > Adult Red Dragon
expected_answer: It exhales fire in a 60-foot cone, recharging on a roll of 5-6. Each creature in the area makes a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 63 (18d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

question: What are the levels of exhaustion and what do they do?
expected_answer: Six levels, each adding to the ones below it: 1 disadvantage on ability checks, 2 speed halved, 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws, 4 hit point maximum halved, 5 speed reduced to 0, 6 death. A creature suffers its current level and all lower levels. Finishing a long rest reduces exhaustion by one level, provided the creature has also eaten and drunk.

question: How much damage do you take from falling?
expected_answer: 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6. The creature lands prone unless it avoids taking damage from the fall.

question: What does the Dodge action do?
expected_answer: Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have disadvantage if the attacker can be seen by you, and you make Dexterity saving throws with advantage. You lose the benefit if you become incapacitated or your speed drops to 0.

question: How is surprise determined at the start of combat, and what happens to a surprised creature?
expected_answer: The GM compares the Dexterity (Stealth) checks of anyone hiding against the passive Wisdom (Perception) of each creature on the other side; anyone who does not notice a threat is surprised at the start of the encounter. If neither side is being stealthy they automatically notice each other. A surprised creature can't move or take an action on its first turn of combat and can't take a reaction until that turn ends. Individual members of a group can be surprised while others are not.

question: How many magic items can a character be attuned to at once?
expected_answer: Three. Any attempt to attune to a fourth fails until the creature ends an existing attunement. An item can be attuned to only one creature at a time, and a creature cannot attune to more than one copy of the same item. Attuning requires spending a short rest in physical contact with the item, focused only on it.

question: What bonus does half cover give?
expected_answer: A +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. A target has half cover if an obstacle blocks at least half its body, which can include another creature, friend or foe. Only the most protective degree of cover applies; degrees never add together.

question: How long does it take to put on heavy armor?
grounding: Armor > Getting Into and Out of Armor
expected_answer: 10 minutes to don heavy armor and 5 minutes to doff it. You benefit from the armor's AC only if you take the full time to don it, and doffing time is halved with help.

question: How do I work out my spell slots if I multiclass as a paladin and a wizard?
expected_answer: Add your full levels in bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer and wizard to half your levels (rounded down) in paladin and ranger, then read your slots off the Multiclass Spellcaster table using that total. Spells known and prepared are still determined class by class as though you were single-classed. The table can grant slots of a higher level than any spell you know; those slots may be used to cast lower-level spells, including at their enhanced higher-level effect.

question: What are the rules for firearms?
expected_answer: The SRD contains no firearm rules; the word does not appear in it. The app should say the SRD does not cover firearms rather than improvising rules from the ranged weapon entries.

question: How do I craft a magic item?
expected_answer: The SRD does not include magic item crafting rules. It has a Magic Items chapter covering attunement, activation and individual item descriptions, but nothing on creating one. The app should say so rather than assembling an answer from the attunement or downtime sections.
